ody.text: Kamahl leaves his mountain home and his sister Jeska for Cabal City to seek wealth and fame as a pit fighter, declaring that he came to win.
He wins sponsorship, first sees the Mirari and befriends Seton and Chainer, then kills a Krosan dragon attacking the city, though Lieutenant Kirtar is credited and takes the Mirari as his prize.

Kamahl partners with Chainer for a record winning streak and refuses the Patriarch's order to throw a match, until the Mirari drives Chainer mad and the dying Chainer gives it to Kamahl, who attaches it to his sword.
Under its influence Kamahl tries to unite the Pardic barbarians by force and mortally wounds his sister Jeska, and he later plants the Mirari in Krosa, where its power mutates the inhabitants.

tor.text: Kamahl befriends Chainer, who is rising through the Cabal with the Mirari, and the two train together as a duo.

When Chainer fills the central arena with dementia beasts and routs the Order's attack, Kamahl is seriously injured, and Chainer heals him with snakeskin, but Kamahl burns his skin off and ruins their friendship.
Kamahl confronts Chainer and melts off his artificial arm, and as the Mirari overwhelms him Chainer begs Kamahl to kill him, so Kamahl does and the Mirari passes to him.
Laquatus then controls Balthor and forces him to fight Kamahl, who kills him at his plea and then kills Laquatus.

jud.text: Kamahl keeps his promise to the dying Chainer by keeping the Mirari safe from others and from himself, but when he returns home it dominates him and he tries to take all the tribes under his dictatorship, dividing the barbarians.
In battle Kamahl impales his sister Jeska with the Mirari-sword, leaving an incurable wound, and shocked, he resolves to be rid of the Mirari.

Balthor sacrifices himself so Kamahl can flee with Jeska into the Krosan forest, where Thriss teaches him druidism, though Laquatus later mind-controls the zombified Balthor into fighting him and Kamahl must strike down his old mentor at his plea.
Kamahl strikes down Laquatus with the Mirari-sword, leaves it in the ground and forsakes the Mirari for a druidic life.

ons.text: Kamahl relocates to the Krosan Forest with the Mirari and becomes a druid of Krosa, leaving the violence of his former life behind him.

When Braids takes Jeska from Seton's hut, Kamahl finds it burned and his sister missing, and when he fights Phage in the pits and she does not recognize him, he stops the match and returns to Krosa to build an army.
Kamahl declares war on Ixidor and leads the Cabal and Krosan alliance against Topos in the Nightmare War, where he defeats his Mirari-possessed persona.
Deathwurms are purged from Phage, but Kamahl must watch his sister become Phage again to bind them, and he meditates in Krosa for a year until Stonebrow revives him with the Soul Reaper.

lgn.text: Kamahl and the Cabal, in an uneasy alliance, set out to defeat Akroma.
After the joint army flees Phage's deathwurms at Topos, Kamahl arrives with the Soul Reaper just as Zagorka jumps from her tower, and the goddess Karona is born.

scg.text: Kamahl feels the full force of the Mirari's pull once again, but he has learned much since the last time.

His Soul Reaper kills Phage, Akroma and Zagorka, whose merged souls become Karona, and he resolves that she must be stopped and retrieves the Mirari from Laquatus's corpse with the help of Balthor's ghost.
Kamahl and the numena confront Karona in Sanctum, where Karona and the numena are killed, and Kamahl frees his sister Jeska.
